sections.text: A dynamic report is a tree of lines with one column per value and period: a stock position by location and product, a sales analysis by customer, a balance sheet. The reporting addon (depends on base and web) holds the report records, resolves the options (dates, comparison, companies, unfolded lines, order), computes the lines and answers the drill-down behind a line or a cell. Every read runs as the caller, in the call's read transaction; nothing is cached between calls. A report names a **provider**. The generic provider reporting.definition reads the report's lines, columns and expressions from data, so most reports need no Rust. An addon whose report cannot be written as data (an aged balance, a ledger) registers a native provider.

<record id="report_stock" model="reporting.report"> <field name="name">Stock Position</field> <field name="date_mode">single</field> <field name="date_default">today</field> <field name="totals_below" eval="True"/> </record> <record id="report_stock_qty" model="reporting.report.column"> <field name="report_id" ref="report_stock"/> <field name="name">On Hand</field> <field name="label">qty</field> <field name="sortable" eval="True"/> </record> <record id="report_stock_line" model="reporting.report.line"> <field name="report_id" ref="report_stock"/> <field name="name">Stock</field> <field name="code">STOCK</field> <field name="groupby">location_id, product_id</field> </record> <record id="report_stock_line_qty" model="reporting.report.expression"> <field name="line_id" ref="report_stock_line"/> <field name="label">qty</field> <field name="model">stock.quant</field> <field name="field">quantity</field> <field name="domain">[["location_id.usage", "=", "internal"]]</field> </record> **Report** (reporting.report): date_mode (range or single), date_default (today in single mode only, this_month, last_month, this_quarter, last_quarter, this_year, last_year), comparison, multi_company, unfold_all, hide_zero (never, optional, by_default), search_bar, totals_below (a total line after the children of an unfolded line) and load_more_limit (children per page, from 10 to the setting reporting.max_load_more_limit). **Columns** (reporting.report.column): label (the expression label the cells show; lower-case, unique in the report), kind (monetary, decimal, integer, percent), scale (0 to 12 decimals; monetary cells use the company currency's), sortable, blank_if_zero, and rollup: none with a rollup_field shows the cell only on lines grouped by that field (quantities of different units are never added up). **Lines** (reporting.report.line): code (upper-case, unique in the report), parent_id, sequence, groupby (direct many2one, char, selection or integer fields of the expression's model, outermost first, at most reporting.max_unfold_depth), foldable (foldable, always_unfolded, never_unfolded), hide_if_zero (the line and its children are left out when all their cells are zero) and optional (left out, and named in hidden_lines, for a caller who may not read its records). A line has child lines or a group-by, not both. **Expressions** (reporting.report.expression), one per label of a line: - aggregate: the sum of field (the record count when empty) over model and domain (a JSON domain), read with read_group as the caller. With date_field, the period applies: strict_range keeps the records of the period, from_beginning everything up to its end (a position). When the model has a company_id, the selected companies apply too, with records of no company. Unfolding groups by the next groupby field with the parent keys in the domain. The aggregate expressions of a grouped line share their model, domain and date. - formula: + - * /, parentheses and numbers over CODE.label (another line), label (the same line, evaluated per group key on grouped lines, which may use only their own labels) and sum_children (the same label of the direct child lines). zero_division is error (the default) or empty. Every save of a definition record checks the whole report; a formula cycle is refused naming its members, an unknown reference when the report is used (a data file may create it in a later record).

use erp_addon_reporting::definition::ReportDef; use erp_addon_reporting::line::{DrillTarget, ExpandPage, Expansion, LineId}; use erp_addon_reporting::options::Options; use erp_addon_reporting::provider::{ProviderSpec, ReportCx, ReportProvider}; use erp_sdk::serde_json::Value as Json; use erp_sdk::{BoxFuture, prelude::*}; pub struct AgedBalance; const SPEC: ProviderSpec = ProviderSpec::new("account.aged_balance", 1); impl ReportProvider for AgedBalance { fn spec(&self) -> &ProviderSpec { &SPEC } fn init_options<'a>(&'a self, cx: &'a mut ReportCx<'_>, report: &'a ReportDef, options: &'a mut Options, strict: bool) -> BoxFuture<'a, Result<()>> { // check and default its own keys in options.provider; refuse an unknown one Box::pin(async move { Ok(()) }) } fn lines<'a>(&'a self, cx: &'a mut ReportCx<'_>, report: &'a ReportDef, options: &'a Options) -> BoxFuture<'a, Result<Expansion>> { todo!() } fn expand<'a>(&'a self, cx: &'a mut ReportCx<'_>, report: &'a ReportDef, options: &'a Options, line: &'a LineId, page: ExpandPage) -> BoxFuture<'a, Result<Expansion>> { todo!() } fn drill<'a>(&'a self, cx: &'a mut ReportCx<'_>, report: &'a ReportDef, options: &'a Options, line: &'a LineId, target: &'a DrillTarget) -> BoxFuture<'a, Result<Json>> { todo!() } } erp_addon_reporting::provider_declarations!(AgedBalance); The report record names it with <field name="provider">account.aged_balance</field>. The registration counts only in a database where the declaring addon is installed; an unknown name is refused by name, and two installed addons with one provider name fail every lookup naming both. - cx.env() and cx.tx() are the caller's environment and transaction. There is no elevated environment: a provider reads as the caller. - lines returns the top-level lines; the runtime unfolds the lines the options ask for by calling expand with the first page, adds the total lines, and refuses an answer over reporting.max_screen_lines (never a cut tree). - expand checks the line id against its report before any query (the segments of a line id come from the browser), returns one page of page.limit children from page.offset and, when more exist, a load-more line last. - drill returns an action result that the web client's action check admits (a window on a record, or a list with a domain).

All four are methods of reporting.report with read effect: | Method | Arguments | Answer | |---|---|---| | erp_report_options | report, previous (options or false) | name, options (previous values kept where they still apply), filters | | erp_report_lines | options | options, lines, hidden_lines, computed_at | | erp_report_expand | options, line_id, offset | lines (one page, then the unfolded lines below) | | erp_report_drill | options, line_id, target ({"item": "open"} or {"cell": n}) | an action | erp_report_lines and the others refuse an unknown option key or a value the report does not offer; options are report, companies (among the caller's allowed companies), date (mode, preset, from, to), comparison (mode: none, previous_period, same_last_year, custom; periods up to reporting.max_comparison_periods; order), unfold_all, unfolded (line ids), hide_zero, search (at most 256 characters), provider and order (column, direction). Each line has id, parent, name, level, kind (section, group, detail, total, more), unfoldable, unfolded, cells (each with kind, value as a decimal string at its scale, currency and zero), caret, and for a load-more line remaining and next_offset.

The report screen is the client action reporting.report (ADR 0234): addons/reporting/static/src/ registers it with registerClientAction, and the action's params name the report ({"report": <id>}; the validator refuses any other key and a report the caller cannot read). A menu for your own report is one record and one menu item: <record id="my_report_action" model="ir.actions.client"> <field name="name">My report</field> <field name="tag">reporting.report</field> <field name="params" eval="{'report': ref('my_report')}"/> </record> <menuitem id="my_report_menu" name="My report" parent="my_app.reports_menu" action="my_report_action"/> The screen asks the four calls above and nothing else. It sends the options it received back whole, so a provider's own provider options and any new shared option pass through without client code. What it shows follows the answers: the filter bar offers only what filters says the report supports, the column heads come from options.columns and options.column_groups, a cell's kind, value, scale and zero decide how it is written, and caret lists the menu items of a line (open is the only one the definition provider makes). A provider that adds a caret item gets a menu entry with that name and the screen calls erp_report_drill with {"item": name}. The behavior of the screen, case by case, is in docs/design/REPORTING.UI-matrix.md. @erpforall/client exports saveFile (offer a blob as a download) and icon for screens of this kind.

The screen's PDF and XLSX buttons call one route, POST /erp/reporting/export. No JSON-2 method returns bytes, so this is a download route like the pivot's (/erp/pivot/export): a browser session (no bearer credentials), a same-origin fetch, Content-Type: application/json, and a body bounded by reporting.export_max_request_bytes (over it: 413 naming the setting). Request body, exactly these three keys (any other key, such as rows or lines, is refused with 422; the browser never posts rows): {"report": 12, "options": {"date": {"preset": "this_month"}, "unfold_all": true, "hide_zero": true, "search": "desk"}, "format": "pdf"} - report: the reporting.report id; options.report may be left out (a different id there is refused). - options: the screen's options, as erp_report_lines takes them (the same strict checks). - format: "pdf" or "xlsx". The server recomputes the lines as the caller, with the unfolded lines the options name (or every line when unfold_all is set), each unfolded within the report's load_more_limit page (a load-more line becomes a row reading "N more"). Hide zero and the search text are applied as the screen applies them: a line stays when it or a line below it is non-zero (text counts as zero); a search keeps the lines whose name contains the text (any case), their ancestors and their descendants; a load-more line follows its parent. The export counts the rows it would write: over reporting.export_max_rows it is a Validation error naming that setting, never a truncated file (larger reports will get durable export jobs in a later release). The unfold step is bounded by the same setting. Answer, 200: | Header | Value | |---|---| | Content-Type | application/pdf, or application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet | | Content-Disposition | attachment with the report name as file name (.pdf or .xlsx) | | Cache-Control | private, no-store | | X-Content-Type-Options | nosniff | Refusals: 401 no session or a bearer credential; 403 a foreign origin or a cross-site fetch, and the ordinary Access refusal when the caller may not read the report or a model behind a line; 405 for another method; 413 a body over the bound; 415 another content type; 422 a bad request or options, or a report over the row bound. 503 names a server composed without the export. - **PDF.** A4, with a header built from the company of the options (its first selected company): logo, name and address, then the report title, the period of each column group and the print time (UTC), then one table whose header repeats on every page. Six or more data columns across all column groups print landscape; five or fewer portrait. Numbers show at their cell's scale, without a thousands separator (the user's number format is not applied yet). The node's report runtime lays the document out (report_job::layout), so a server without a render worker answers User ("Printing is not available"). - **XLSX.** One sheet: a period row (merged over each column group's columns), a column-name row, then one row per line with the name indented by its level, bold for sections and totals, numbers stored as numbers with their decimals. A second sheet, "Options", lists the options used (nested keys joined with a dot) and the optional lines the caller may not read. Text is always a string cell: a name starting with =, +, -, @, a tab or a carriage return carries the quote-prefix flag and no cell of the file is a formula. A native provider needs nothing: the export reads the same lines it returns to the screen. To build a file in Rust use reporting::export::prepare (it parses the same body) and Prepared::xlsx or Prepared::document.

Declared in the block "Dynamic reports" of the Settings page, each with a default, a floor and a hard bound: | Setting | Default | Range | |---|---|---| | reporting.max_load_more_limit | 2000 | 10 to 2000 | | reporting.max_unfold_depth | 8 | 2 to 16 | | reporting.max_screen_lines | 10000 | 500 to 50000 | | reporting.max_comparison_periods | 12 | 1 to 16 | | reporting.export_max_rows | 50000 | 100 to 500000 | | reporting.export_max_request_bytes | 1048576 | 16384 to 16777216 |

Internal users read the report records; administrators create and change them. A report's numbers are read with the caller's rights: a record rule narrows every line, group and drill-down list, and a line over a model or field the caller may not read is an Access refusal, never a zero, unless the line is optional.
